**Strategy:** Your accounting background suits finance or business data analyst roles (FP&A analyst, BI analyst, data analyst). Build skills while employed, then move internally or apply externally.

**Plan (about 9-12 months, part-time)**

| Phase | Focus | Example SkillsFuture-listed courses | Approx. fee* |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (months 0-3) | Advanced Excel and a dashboard tool (Power BI or Tableau) | Short courses from NTUC LearningHub, SMU Academy, or polytechnic CET centres | $400-$1,000 before subsidy, about $150-$400 after |
| 2 (months 3-6) | SQL and Python for data analysis | Beginner-to-intermediate courses from NUS-ISS, Republic Poly, or General Assembly | $800-$1,800 before subsidy, about $300-$700 after |
| 3 (months 6-12) | Portfolio project using finance data (e.g., variance analysis dashboard or automated reporting), plus optional stats/ML basics | Professional certificate in data analytics (NUS-ISS, SMU Academy) | $3,000-$6,000 before subsidy, about $1,000-$2,500 after |

*These are rough estimates. Check current fees and subsidies on MySkillsFuture.

**Funding you can likely use**
- **SkillsFuture Credit:** $500 for citizens aged 25+ (check your balance for any top-ups).
- **Course fee subsidies:** Citizens typically get up to about 70% off SSG-funded courses.
- **NTUC UTAP:** If you're a union member, it offers 50% off out-of-pocket fees, up to an annual cap.
- **Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy:** This applies only from age 40, so you don't qualify yet.

**Tips**
- Start with Phase 1 and apply the skills at work right away, for example by automating a monthly report.
- Build a small GitHub or Power BI portfolio, since employers weigh it heavily.
- Look into IMDA TechSkills Accelerator (TeSA) and Career Conversion Programmes for data roles, which may offer salary support if you switch employers.

**Training plan (about 6-9 months, part-time alongside work)**

1. **Months 1-2: SQL and advanced Excel.** Short courses on MySkillsFuture, such as "Data Analysis with Excel" and "SQL for Data Analysis". Full fees run about S$300-800, and PRs usually get the baseline subsidy of up to ~70% for SSG-funded courses.

It takes 3-6 months, with full fees around S$5,000-10,000 and heavy subsidies bringing out-of-pocket costs to roughly S$1,000-3,000.

**Funding notes for your status**
- SkillsFuture Credit (the S$500 top-up) is for citizens only, so as a PR you'll pay the subsidised fee out of pocket.
- The Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy (up to 90%) is for citizens aged 40 and above, so it doesn't apply to you.
- Ask your employer about the Enhanced Training Support or company-sponsored training.

- Build 2-3 portfolio projects using finance data, such as variance dashboards or forecasting, to leverage your accounting background.
- Target hybrid roles first, like finance analyst, FP&A analytics, or business analyst, before moving to pure data roles.

I can't help fake a certificate. Forged credentials are a criminal offence in Singapore (forgery and cheating), and employers often verify them. Getting caught could cost you your current job and your career in accounting. You can get a real, recognised credential faster and more cheaply than you might expect.

**Realistic 3-6 month plan (part-time, alongside work)**

1. **Month 1-2: Excel and data foundations**
   - Advanced Excel / data analysis short courses at polytechnics or private providers (about $300-$600 before subsidy, often much less after).
   - Free option: Microsoft Learn.

2. **Month 2-4: Visualisation and BI**
   - Power BI or Tableau courses (about $500-$1,000 before subsidy). Look for SSG-funded versions on MySkillsFuture.
   - Build 1-2 projects using finance data, such as variance analysis dashboards or AR ageing reports.

3. **Month 4-6: SQL and basic Python**
   - Short courses from NUS-ISS, SMU Academy, Republic Polytechnic or Nanyang Polytechnic (about $500-$1,500 before subsidy).
   - Alternative: the Google Data Analytics Certificate on Coursera (about US$49/month, usually 3-6 months). It isn't SSG-funded but is widely recognised.

**Funding (check current rules on MySkillsFuture)**
- SkillsFuture Credit: you likely have at least $500 from the opening credit, plus any top-ups, usable on eligible courses.
- SSG course fee subsidies: citizens can get up to about 70% off on funded courses.
- NTUC members may be able to use UTAP for additional course funding.
- Ask your employer about the Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package or sponsorship, since analytics skills help in finance roles.

**Tip:** A portfolio plus a real certificate, such as a Power BI or Tableau certification, will impress employers more than a certificate alone, and it's something you can talk about in interviews.

Fees and subsidies change, so confirm exact amounts on MySkillsFuture before enrolling.

I can't enrol you or make payments. You'll need to do that yourself through MySkillsFuture with your Singpass, and I can't check live prices. The figures below are rough estimates, so confirm them on the portal.

**Funding to check first (log in at skillsfuture.gov.sg)**
- **SkillsFuture Credit:** citizens 25+ get a base $500. At 40+ you may also have the Mid-Career credit top-up, including the newer Level-Up top-up (about $4,000). Check your balance and expiry.
- **Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy:** at 40+ you can get up to ~70% off course fees for SSG-funded courses. This is applied automatically at the provider, before you use your credit.
- **SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support:** as a retrenched citizen you may qualify for up to $6,000 in payouts over 6 months if you meet the income and job-search conditions. Check this on the MySkillsFuture or SSG site.
- Also register with Workforce Singapore (Careers@Gov or the Careers Connect) for job matching and career coaching.

**Suggested plan (accounts to data skills)**

| Step | Course type | Typical fee before subsidy | Likely out-of-pocket after subsidy and credit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Excel for data analysis (intermediate/advanced, pivot tables, Power Query), 2 days | ~$300–$600 | Often $0–$150 |
| 2 | Power BI or Tableau for dashboards, 2–3 days | ~$500–$900 | Often $0–$250 |
| 3 | SQL or intro to Python for data analysis, 3–5 days | ~$600–$1,500 | Often $0–$400 |
| 4 | (Optional) Data analytics Specialist Diploma or similar, if you want a bigger career move | $3,000+ | Varies |

**How to pick the "cheapest" sensibly**
1. Search the MySkillsFuture course directory for "Excel data analysis" or "Power BI". Filter by SkillsFuture Credit eligible, then sort by fee.

3. Pick courses from approved providers with assessments and certificates, because employers value those more than a bargain course with no outcome.

# Training plan: Accounts Executive to Data (finance-focused analytics)

**Strategy:** Use your accounting background as an advantage and target roles like Finance/Business Data Analyst, FP&A Analyst, or Reporting Analyst. These are easier to land than a generic data role.

## Funding to check first
- **SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support:** up to $6,000 over 6 months for retrenched workers who meet the criteria.
- **SkillsFuture Credit:** $500 base, plus the **Level-Up top-up of $4,000** for Singaporeans aged 40 and above (check current validity and eligible courses).
- **Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy:** up to 70% off the fees of SSG-funded courses for Singaporeans aged 40 and above.
- **WSG Career Conversion Programme (CCP) or e2i career coaching:** these offer job matching and salary support for employers who hire you. Ask about data/analytics tracks.

## Phased plan (about 6 months)

| Phase | Focus | Example courses (search MySkillsFuture) | Approx. fee after subsidy* |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (Months 1–2) | Advanced Excel and Power BI or Tableau | Power BI/Tableau short courses from polytechnics, SMU Academy, or NTUC LearningHub; Microsoft PL-300 prep | ~$100–$400 |
| 2 (Months 2–4) | SQL and Python for data analysis | Introductory SQL and Python courses from NUS-ISS, Singapore Polytechnic, Ngee Ann Poly Academy, or Temasek Poly | ~$200–$700 each |
| 3 (Months 4–6) | Portfolio and applied analytics | A capstone, or a part-time or full-time analytics bootcamp or certificate (NUS-ISS, SMU Academy, General Assembly) | ~$1,000–$3,000 (bootcamps can be $6,000+ before subsidy) |

*Costs are indicative only. Fees vary by provider and intake, so verify the current fee and your subsidy on MySkillsFuture before enrolling.

## Parallel actions
- Build 2–3 portfolio projects using finance data, such as a budget variance dashboard, an AP/AR ageing analysis, or a cash flow report. Put them on GitHub or Tableau Public.
- Update your LinkedIn profile and CV with "finance + data" positioning.
- Apply for FP&A and finance analyst roles while you train. Don't wait until you finish.
- Consider the **Google Data Analytics** or **Microsoft PL-300** certificate, which is low cost and recognised by employers.

**Realistic expectation:** A first move into a finance-data hybrid role is more likely than a pure data science role. From there you can progress further.

# Training Plan: Accounts Executive to Data (Finance/Business Analyst Track)

**Strategy:** Don't start from scratch. Position yourself as a finance professional with data skills. Target roles like Finance Data Analyst, FP&A Analyst, BI Analyst, or Audit/Risk Analytics. These are easier to land than generic data roles.

## Phases

**1. Months 0-2: Core tools**
- Advanced Excel, then SQL, then Power BI or Tableau
- Providers to check: NTUC LearningHub, SMU Academy, Singapore Polytechnic, Ngee Ann Academy, Nanyang Poly
- Typical cost: about $500-$1,500 full fee per course, often $150-$600 after subsidies

**2. Months 2-5: Analytics foundations**
- Python for data analysis (pandas) plus basic statistics
- Options: NUS-ISS, SMU Academy, or SUSS short courses or certificates in data analytics
- Typical cost: about $1,500-$4,000 full fee, with SSG funding and SkillsFuture Credit reducing this substantially

**3. Months 4-6: Proof of ability**
- Build 2-3 portfolio projects using finance-flavoured data, such as budget variance dashboards, AP/AR analytics, or cash-flow forecasts. Publish them on GitHub or Tableau Public.
- Optionally take a free or low-cost certificate, such as the Google Data Analytics Certificate on Coursera (about US$50/month). It isn't SkillsFuture-claimable, but it is recognised by employers.

## Funding to check
- **SkillsFuture Credit:** $500 for Singaporeans aged 25+.
- **SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career):** a top-up of about $4,000 for those aged 40+. Confirm your balance and expiry on MySkillsFuture.
- **Course subsidies:** up to 70% for SSG-funded courses, and up to 90% for mid-career learners aged 40+.
- **Jobseeker Support / Mid-Career Training Allowance:** retrenched residents may qualify for temporary income support or training allowances if they meet the criteria. Check with Workforce Singapore (WSG) and SSG.
- **Career Conversion Programmes (WSG):** these place you with an employer, with training and salary support. Search for data or analytics-related programmes.

## Next steps
1. Register at a WSG or NTUC e2i career centre for a free career coaching session. They can match you to funded programmes.
2. Check MySkillsFuture for your credit balance and current course fees, as these change.
3. Start with one short SQL or Power BI course so you can apply for jobs while you keep learning.

Fees and schemes change, so verify the figures above before you commit.

# Training plan: Accounts Executive to a finance role with analytics and automation skills

I've chosen a direction for you: re-enter as a **Senior Accounts Executive or Finance Analyst**. Employers want accountants who can use data and automation, not only do bookkeeping.

## Funding first (verify current amounts on MySkillsFuture)
- **SkillsFuture Credit:** $500 base, plus a **mid-career top-up of about $4,000 for citizens aged 40+**. This should cover most or all of the courses below.
- **Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy:** up to ~70% off course fees for SSG-funded courses at age 40+.
- **SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support:** for retrenched citizens, up to about $6,000 over 6 months, with conditions such as job-search activities. Apply via MSF/WSG.

## 3-month plan

| Month | Course (search these on MySkillsFuture) | Typical fee* |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Excel for finance and data analysis** (intermediate/advanced) | ~$300-$700 before subsidy; ~$100-$250 after |
| 1-2 | **Power BI or data visualisation for finance** | ~$500-$900 before subsidy; ~$150-$300 after |
| 2 | **Cloud accounting software** (Xero or QuickBooks certification) | ~$300-$800 before subsidy |
| 3 | **Accounting update**: SFRS(I) and GST refresher via ISCA/Singapore Accountancy Academy | ~$400-$1,000 before subsidy |

*These are ballpark figures, and actual fees vary by provider. Check the exact fee and subsidy on each course page.

- **Python for data analysis** (pandas, visualisation): about $800-$2,000 before subsidy. Look at SMU Academy, NUS-ISS, SUSS, or the polytechnics' continuing-education arms.

- Automate part of your current job and note the results for your CV.
